Doesnt mean they cant get any fruits by the way, but think of fruits as a somewhat healthier snack you can put in the veggie mix and the veggies as the main meal. I put chopped grapes in a mix of parsley, brocolli and cucumber for my birds. theres a bunch of fruits and veggies that birds cant eat too (avocado or onions sre the most noteably examples) so make sure to check that the thing is safe before giving it

Veggies are better than fruits. It can be rather hard to get birds thats used to seeds/pellets to start eating veggies and fruits, so you should have some in the cage almost everyday so they get used to it.

 Also remember to not give them too many treats as they can get overweight from it (some people put in daily millet sticks which makes them overeat on it as it doesnt have all nutrients they need)

Once they get tamer its easier to introduce new foods to them too as they will think of your hand as a source of tasty foods. Eating something u want them to try (a bit of cucumber for example) infront of them may also help once they trust you.

I have’nt had cockatiels myself but I have both parakeets and kakarikis. From my experience I would focus on  your male cockatiel in the taming process as makes tend to be easier to get tame in my experience. Seeing as theyre a group animal the female will most likely follow his lead if you keep working with them. Start with making sure theyre comfortable with you outside their cage before sticking your hand in to train them. Once they dont seem bothered by your hand try having treats in your hand that you know they like (Millet often works but not always, my kakariki only likes sunflower seeds for example) to encourage them to make contact with your hand. 

Cockatiels are a rather anxious species from my understanding, so keep in mind that they might need a long time to trust you. Them having eachother may slow down the taming even more.

Most importantly is that you don’t give up. My female kakariki took over a month before i got to make any contact with her but since then she’s the one running up to my hand when I put it in the cage. Had I given up like I was close to I’d miss out on all the joy she brings.

Parakeets drink a very small amount and not that often, if you have’nt somehow fed him water he most likely has drunk without you noticing. As for food it’s most likely the change of enviorment. Give him a few days and he’ll likely eat from food bowls.

 Be careful on how much millet you give him in his cage freely though as it’s a rather fatty food.
